pages.title: Validation report — CyTools_AudioLibrary 0.1.0 (2026-09-21)
pages.html:
Validation report — CyTools_AudioLibrary 0.1.0 (2026-09-21)#

Everything below was executed on one machine: Windows 10 x64 (build 10.0.19044), Ryzen 9 7900X, 127 GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 24 GB (driver 610.47), CPython 3.12.0, PyTorch 2.8.0+cu126, transformers 4.57.6, imgui-bundle 1.92.900, CyToolsCore 0.9.0. The evidence files named below are written to data/reports/ on the validation machine and are not part of the repository: they list the files of a personal sound library. Three kinds of statement are kept apart: real run, fixtures, not verified.

1. Real runs (real weights, real audio, CUDA)#

Real library used: 107 WAV files referenced read-only from three existing folders (5 captioned Clotho clips shipped with the pinned Omni-Embed-Audio source, 77 files of C:\Windows\Media, 25 sounds generated earlier by CyTools_AudioGen). It is small and WAV-only: it proves the pipeline and gives an indication of relevance, not a benchmark.

What Result Evidence
Model installation through the Tool (install_model): M2D-CLAP 2025 (1.47 GB zip, SHA-256 from the GitHub release digest, resumed from a partial file), LAION-CLAP (0.6 GB), Qwen3-1.7B (4.1 GB), Omni-Embed-Audio Qwen3B-Cl + Qwen2.5-Omni-3B thinker shards (19.5 GB) 4/4 Installed, receipts with per-file SHA-256 and model hash install-*.json
Scan + metadata + loudness + waveform pyramid 107 files, 0 failure; rescan: 107 unchanged in 0.03 s; 2 exact duplicate groups found real-m2d-clap.json
M2D-CLAP 2025 embeddings (whole clip + 10 s windows, 2 s overlap) 107 files in 9.8 s including model load real-m2d-clap.json
Omni-Embed-Audio Qwen3B-Cl embeddings 107 files in 32 s including ~20 s load of the 9.5 GB checkpoint real-three-models.json
Caption → file retrieval on the 5 captioned clips (rank of the expected file) M2D alone 3/5 top-1, 5/5 top-2 · M2D + LAION 4/5 top-1 · M2D + LAION + Omni 4/5 top-1 (ranks 2,1,1,1,1) same files
Warm text search, three models, 107 files 0.08–0.12 s per query real-three-models.json
Qwen3-1.7B query understanding (French requests → English structured query) 1.2–1.8 s warm; 7.8–16.6 s on the first call (model load). "gros impact métallique très lourd avec une longue réverbération" → heavy metal impact with long reverb real-m2d-laion-qwen3.json, library-search-fr.png
Interface scenario: French query with a negation → LLM → three models → RRF water_stream.wav first at 70 % (67 / 73 / 70), every other file ≤ 22 % library-search-fr.png, .json
Measured VRAM (resident): M2D 0.75 GiB, LAION-CLAP 0.6 GiB, Omni-Embed 3B 8.9 GiB; 10.3 GiB peak with the three loaded catalogue estimates lowered to 2 / 1.5 / 11 GiB real-three-models.json
Measured cosines, unrelated vs matching: M2D 0.16 vs 0.30, LAION 0.03 vs 0.38–0.48, Omni 0.05 vs 0.62–0.83 display ranges set from these values catalogue similarityRange
Launcher: CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe started from C:\ interface opened with the private pythonw, 107 rows, waveform, decoded audio, details job library-en.json/.png
ImGui tabs rendered: Library EN and FR, Options EN and FR, Application log, Advanced operations screenshots saved, exit code 0 *.png
CLI describe, invoke install_model, invoke of every operation used above —
Real MCP: official mcp stdio client → server → jobs 8 expected tools present, real two-model search (9.4 s cold), InvalidParameters and LicenseAcceptanceRequired returned as job errors mcp-validation.json
Engine update check against the real upstream repositories both sources at their pinned revision console output, §UPDATES
Fine tuned query assistant cytools-search-assist@v1 (Qwen2.5-1.5B + LoRA, trained on Colab A100 in 3.9 min, merged locally) 250/250 validation answers are valid JSON with the expected shape; agreement with the reference answers 92.0 % on categories, 83.2 % on tags search-assist-finetune.json, finetune-train_report.json
Retrieval with that model, 150 messy multilingual queries replayed through the real engine on 5 764 files top-5 hit 58.0 % raw query → 89.3 % with its caption → 95.3 % with caption and variations search-assist-finetune.json
Category hint re-ordering, 250 queries, hintBoost swept 0 / 0.06 / 0.12 / 0.25 first place 72.8 → 84.4 → 87.2 → 89.2 %; default kept at 0.12. Measures agreement with the Library's own automatic categories, not perceptual relevance search-assist-finetune.json
Both prompt profiles end to end through the CLI caption: 4 captions, 2 categories resolved, 46 candidates re-ordered, 8.5 s cold. generic with Qwen3-1.7B: unchanged behaviour, no hints search-assist-finetune.json
Interface, real run: --ui-test-library with "il me faudrait des pas ds la neige bien proche, pas de musique", fine tune selected, 5 764 files status line reads `LLM cytools-search-assist@v1 (8.52 s) category hints: 16 results reordered`; results dominated by snow and footsteps files; waveform, decoded audio and details loaded
Fine tune made the default model, for the interface, the CLI and MCP at once search_sounds with neither llmAssist nor llmModel resolved to cytools-search-assist@v1, profile caption, 7.99 s; the interface opened on Auto with it selected, 313 candidates re-ordered search-assist-default.png, -ui.json
Folders, selection and batch edits in the interface, 5 764 files folder tree with recursive counts, 4 sounds selected, Selection (4) tab with the batch editor; single-sound view with category picker, description and notes selection-batch.png, selection-single.png
Folders over real MCP op_list_folders: 4 roots, 42 top-level folders; the largest holds 645 files and op_browse_assets with the same rootIds + folderPrefix returns 645; op_update_assets with an empty filter refused (InvalidParameters) mcp-validation.json
CySearchAssist 1.5B and 0.5B installed from Hugging Face through install_model (GGUF Q8_0, pinned revisions, SHA-256 of the manifests) both Installed, verify_model true before and after the dequantised copy was written search-assist-gguf.json
The GGUF models through the Tool's adapter, 250 held out queries 1.5B: 250/250 valid, categories 92.6 %, 3.4 s warm, 3.36 GiB VRAM. 0.5B: 250/250 valid, 82.1 %, 2.2 s, 1.19 GiB search-assist-gguf.json
Loading a GGUF model first load 46 s (1.5B) and 35 s (0.5B) to dequantise; second load 1.6 s and 0.7 s from _dequantized/, same answers search-assist-gguf.json
Retrieval with the 1.5B, same 150 queries, all runs on this machine except the first top 5 with caption + variations: float16 on Colab 95.3 %, float16 here 94.0 %, GGUF Q8_0 here 92.0 % search-assist-gguf.json
Scale, synthetic: 20 000 WAV files scan + metadata + waveforms 62 s; rescan 1.1 s; 40 000 embeddings through the worker protocol 120 s (test adapter, CPU); list 20 000 ids 16 ms; filtered list 16 ms; search over 2 × 20 000 vectors 0.09–0.11 s; cache 46 MB; audio folder untouched scale-test.json

2. Fixture tests (app/tests, 46 tests, all passing; no PyTorch, no weights)#

Real CyToolsCore runtime, real worker process and protocol, synthetic audio, deterministic test adapter. WAV 16/24-bit/float, FLAC, OGG, AIFF, MP3 and M4A/AAC decoding and metadata; known peak/RMS of a sine; waveform pyramid and zoomed read; audio folders byte-identical after scan; external cache; incremental rescan (moved keeps its AudioId, modified re-analysed, missing flagged, new added); two models with different dimensions in separate stores; nothing recomputed on a second run; RRF weights; segment hit inside a long file; filters; similar and selection search; LLM assist and parser fallback; user tags/rating survive re-analysis and re-labelling; a second version of a model coexists and only it is computed; custom model files never deleted; pause → Busy for a second maintenance job → resume; cancellation during a model request: worker process confirmed dead before the job reports Cancelled, next run resumes; error codes; client B cannot read or cancel client A's job; cache move (previous copy kept, cache inside an audio folder refused); exact and probable duplicates; configuration save/load round-trip, no job started by loading, replay through the runtime; French catalogue complete for every interface string; both answer schemas of the query assistant, including a garbled answer and a suggestion that no Library has; the default model resolution, including a configured model that was uninstalled; folder tree counts equal to what the same folder filter returns, one folder edited through filters (tags, categories added and removed, a note appended after the existing one) while the rest of the Library stays untouched, an empty filter refused instead of editing everything; multi-selection (click, Ctrl, Shift, Ctrl+Shift, Ctrl+A, Escape, list order, a new list dropping sounds it no longer shows); update staging, 7 hostile/wrong archives and a symlink entry rejected, activation, rollback, data/ preserved, no repository invented.

3. Not verified — do not assume#

  • Linux and macOS: never executed. CyTools_AudioLibrary.sh and install_linux.sh are untested text.
  • Audible playback and mouse gestures (zoom, pan, drag selection, loop, Space/Up/Down): the code ran (decode, stream setup path, rendering), but no automated test can hear or drag. A person must try them.
  • Real MP3/FLAC/OGG/M4A libraries: formats are covered by fixtures only; the real library was WAV.
  • Large real libraries: the 20 000-file figure is synthetic, 0.25 s files, test adapter. Real GPU throughput on tens of thousands of real files was not measured (extrapolating M2D: roughly 10–15 files/s on this GPU).
  • Segment-level retrieval on real long recordings, and the temporal-order bonus: fixtures only.
  • Real models on CPU: not run. CPU path exercised with the test adapter only.
  • Gated-model flow (401/403, stored token): no gated model was available; the token store command and the error mapping are implemented, not exercised against a provider.
  • Application update from a real GitHub release: the repository MrMybal/CyTools_AudioLibrary is declared, but it holds no release and, on 2026-09-26, it answered 404 to an anonymous request, so it is private or empty. The real check was run and reports exactly that. Download, staging and activation are proved with fixtures only. Staging/activating a newer engine-source revision: not exercised (upstream had none).
  • M2D-CLAP 2024, Omni-Embed-Audio Qwen3B-AC, Qwen3-0.6B/4B: catalogue entries on validated adapters, never installed.
  • The GGUF build of the fine tuned assistant: the quantised file was not part of the Colab download, and the Tool has no llama.cpp adapter, so nothing was loaded from it. The model used here is the adapter merged locally into Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct.
  • A second training run: every fine tune figure comes from one run, on one seed. Nothing was repeated, so the numbers carry no error bar.
  • Audio Flamingo 3 / Deep mode: not implemented (registry entry and capability slots only).
  • LUFS values were not compared with a reference meter. Redistributable installer without a system Python: not provided.

3b. Additions of the second request (same day)#

  • Real run (MCP): search without libraryId returned water_stream.wav (71 %) with its absolute path and Library name; check_library on the real Library: 107 unchanged, nothing written; suggest_names (read-only) on real generically named files, e.g. sound_01.wav → Explosions_Slam_Hit_Reverberant.wav; rename_files without confirm refused; 57 MCP tools listed.
  • Fixtures (24 tests now): background check, cross-Library search, rename + undo, tag writing in six formats with bit-identical decoded audio.
  • Deliberately not executed: rename_files and write_metadata on any real folder of this machine. They change original files and nobody asked for a specific real file to be changed. First real use should be on a few files, with the backup on.
  • Not verified: the ask banner and a complete automatic update cycle seen by a person; tags read back by another application (only mutagen read them); very large files (the rewrite needs free space for one copy next to the file).

4. Problems found during validation, and what was done#

  1. Licence acceptance is personal and cannot be delegated. install_model refuses a model whose licence requires acceptance until acceptLicense is set by the person installing it, the interface never pre-ticks that box, and the MCP test asserts that an installation without acceptance is refused with LicenseAcceptanceRequired.
  2. A folder named aux (reserved on Windows) broke the first install → renamed support.
  3. M2D-CLAP 2025 needs flat_features=True (upstream Example_4): first analysis failed on every file → adapter fixed, and a circuit breaker now stops an analysis when nothing ever succeeds instead of failing the whole Library.
  4. The Omni-Embed checkpoint is a Linux training pickle containing PosixPath objects: unloadable on Windows → loaded with an inert path class inside the worker only; upstream appears untested on Windows.
  5. Auto-labelling with an absolute cosine threshold labelled almost everything (14 "Weapons" among Windows sounds) → replaced by softmax zero-shot over the label set (3 left, shown with model and probability). Model errors remain.
  6. Qwen3-1.7B invented an exclusion ("music") copied from a prompt example → exclusions are kept only when the request contains a negation.
  7. pip replaced the CUDA PyTorch by a newer CPU wheel through a transitive dependency → constraints file + check.
  8. One transient TLS failure (self-signed certificate in certificate chain) on the first PyPI install; a retry succeeded and certificate verification was never disabled. Worth knowing on networks that inspect TLS.

pages.title: Capability coverage — CyTools_AudioLibrary 0.1.0
pages.html:
Capability coverage — CyTools_AudioLibrary 0.1.0#

Status vocabulary: T implemented and tested by a real run on the validation machine · F implemented and tested with fixtures only (synthetic audio, deterministic test adapter) · I implemented, not validated · X not implemented (extension point or exclusion, reason given). Evidence files are written to data/reports/ on the validation machine and are not part of the repository; fixture tests are app/tests/. The numbers in the first column are those of the functional brief.

# Requested capability Operation / field → code Standalone control Status and evidence
2 Virtual Library, several folders, recursive, never copies create_library, add_folder, remove_folder, set_folder_enabled, scan_library.rootIds → audiolib/library.py, scanner.py left panel: New Library, Add Folder, checkbox, right-click Rescan/Open/Remove T real-m2d-clap.json (3 real folders) · F test_01 asserts the audio folders are byte-for-byte untouched
3, 44 Cache fully separate, configurable, movable, per model create_library.cacheLocation, move_cache → Library.cache, move_cache New Library > Cache folder; Cache header > Move Cache F test_01 (external cache), test_13 (move, previous copy kept, cache inside an audio folder refused)
4, 47 Stable AudioId; new/unchanged/modified/moved/missing/duplicate; incremental scan_library → scanner.scan (size + fast hash, SHA-256 on demand) Rescan All / Rescan Folder F test_04: moved keeps its id, only new+modified re-analysed · T rescan of 107 real files: 107 unchanged in 0.03 s
5 WAV, FLAC, MP3, OGG, M4A/AAC, AIFF audiolib/audiofile.py (libsndfile + PyAV, no external ffmpeg) — F test_02: one file per format decoded, duration/bit depth/channels/rate checked · T real WAV only (no real MP3/M4A library was available)
6, 10 Asset database, levels, user fields browse_assets, get_asset, update_assets → database.py; BS.1770 LUFS in audiofile.LoudnessMeter Asset Info tab; Tags and Categories tab (tags, rating, favourite) T screenshot library-en.png (Peak/RMS/LUFS of a real file) · F test_02 peak −6.02 dBFS / RMS −9.03 dBFS of a known sine. LUFS not cross-checked against a reference meter

pages.title: Modular CyUI integration
pages.html:
Modular CyUI integration#

The standalone application uses CyUI 1.2.0, pinned to ff023e6.

Selected modules and replacements#

Core; AudioViews; Plots; Canvas; Diagnostics.

  • The selected-sound waveform uses AudioViews for waveform drawing, playhead, navigation and selection.
  • The host still chooses/cache-reads peak pyramid levels and raw sample detail. A click seeks after release; a drag selects without seeking.
  • Structured logs use Diagnostics, with the original character-selectable text and full-file copy retained.
  • Core replaces the private palette, styles, fonts and common widget implementations. ui_style.py handles host translation, action naming, filter chips and wrapping banners.

Reproducible source and delivery#

app/cyui-source.json records every selected upstream file and its SHA-256. app/cyui.py and app/cyui_modules/*.py are unchanged official sources, normalized to LF. Do not edit them: host adapters live outside the library. Refresh only from the exact pinned checkout:

sh
python app/scripts/sync_cyui.py /path/to/CyUI

The sources are included with the application using its existing source-vendoring mechanism. Neither a developer checkout elsewhere on disk nor an editable pip installation is needed. There is one imgui-bundle renderer, at the version pinned in app/requirements.txt; no C++ umbrella, CMake demo/gallery, CEF, extra model, AI engine, NumPy installation or browser dependency is introduced by this migration. Existing application/DSP/rendering dependencies are kept where required.

Keep LICENCES/CyUI-MIT.txt with the product. The application's own license does not change. The Options licenses list identifies the upstream revision and source.

Host responsibilities and retained adaptations#

The searchable/sortable audio table, ranked search matches, tag edits, file operations and OS drag/drop remain host-owned. CyUI Assets does not represent ranked multi-model matches, editable analysis columns and the existing file-transfer contract. These are not replaced by a less capable generic browser. Peak decoding, sample storage, player state and file bounds remain in the host. No Audio, Nodes or browser runtime is added.

SDK operations, permissions, exclusive groups, temporary AI task files, model installation, licenses/acceptance, generation recipes and Undo remain host-owned. No CyToolsCore runtime or AI library is copied into CyUI. English remains the default and French the persistent selectable second language.

Verification#

63 unit/integration tests; native library and options views. The waveform integration tests exercise real mouse click/release and drag/release.

Run the adapter tests from app/ with the private Python:

sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_modular_ui.py -v

They verify pinned-source integrity, bounded log refresh/redaction and native ImGui frames across five themes, both densities, EN/FR and scale 1.0/1.5/2.0, plus the application-specific data/edit routing. This simulated DPI check is not a physical multi-monitor test. Windows native views are tested locally. Linux/macOS remain unverified by this migration; the source integration stays platform-independent.

Windows packages include the migrated sources and their license notices.

Final local results: 63 unittest tests passed; the native Library/Options views rendered, including the waveform and time ruler in a light theme and in French/navy/comfortable. Real ImGui mouse tests verify click-to-seek versus drag-to-select.

CyUI license: https://github.com/MrMybal/CyUI/blob/main/LICENSE. The complete MIT text ships with the application, including when the upstream repository is private.

pages.title: Updates: three separate streams
pages.html:
Updates: three separate streams#

Stream Source Mechanism Where
Application (app/) GitHub releases of MrMybal/CyTools_AudioLibrary, declared as repository in app/release.json; the Updates tab can override it for a fork, and nothing else is ever guessed. The check is anonymous, so the repository must be public cytools-app.zip + cytools-app.zip.sha256 staged in runtime/updates/tool/<sha256>/
Engine sources nttcslab/m2d, JudeJiwoo/Omni-Embed-Audio, exact revisions pinned in app/engine.json git ls-remote, clone of one revision staged in runtime/updates/engine/<name>/<revision>/
Model weights the catalogue (app/models/catalog.json: pinned revision, size, SHA-256) Installation tab / install_model data/models/

The PyTorch environment is not an update stream: a new pin in engine.json is installed into a new folder with setup_backend.py --environment runtime/engines/<name> --no-activate, then activated by data/settings/backend.json; the previous environment stays for rollback.

Expected application release#

A release of the Tool's repository carries two assets:

  • cytools-app.zip — a single top-level folder app/ (no data/, no runtime/, no weights, no symlink);
  • cytools-app.zip.sha256 — the SHA-256 of the archive (first token of the file).

app/release.json of the archive must name toolId: cy.tool.audiolibrary and the same runtime_abi as the installed application; a release that needs new dependencies changes runtime_abi and is refused with a message asking for a full installation.

Checks before anything becomes pending: URL under the configured repository, SHA-256, archive size limit, no absolute path / drive letter / .. / backslash / symlink entry, manifest identity, ABI, required files, no data folder. Activation happens only at the next start (runtime/bootstrap.py → apply_pending), never while a model worker is alive; the previous app/ is kept in runtime/backups/app/ and Roll back application re-stages it. data/ is never part of a replacement.

Limits, stated plainly#

  • No GitHub repository exists for this Tool: check/download against a real release was not executed. Staging, the hostile-archive rejections, activation, rollback and data preservation are tested with fixture archives (tests/test_maintenance.py).
  • The engine-source check was executed against the real upstream repositories (both at their pinned revision on the validation day, so stage/activate/rollback of a newer revision was not exercised for real; the code path is covered by the same rename-and-backup logic as the application).
  • A checksum published next to a release is not an independent signature of its author.
  • An engine-source update does not change the analysis key (it is keyed on the model, not on the inference code). After activating new engine sources, validate with a real search and roll back if an adapter fails.

Staging, the hostile-archive rejections, activation, rollback and data preservation are tested with fixture archives ( tests/test_maintenance.py ). The engine-source check was executed against the real upstream repositories (both at their pinned revision on the validation day, so stage/activate/rollback of a newer revision was not exercised for real; the code path is covered by the same rename-and-backup logic as the application). A checksum published next to a release is not an independent signature of its author. An engine-source update does not change the analysis key (it is keyed on the model, not on the inference code). After activating new engine sources, validate with a real search and roll back if an adapter fails.

pages.title: Publishing the CyDoc reader
pages.html:
Publishing the CyDoc reader#

The web manual and the embedded manual are the same complete CyDoc HTML export. Markdown files remain editable sources; GitHub Pages serves the generated reader, including its navigation, full-text search, locales, styles, scripts and local media.

Regenerate and stage#

From the repository root, with Node.js 22+ and Python 3.11+:

sh
python app/documentation/build.py --install --checkpython app/tests/test_documentation.pypython app/tests/test_pages.pypython app/documentation/publish.py

The locked, vendored CyDoc package provides the generator. CI needs no access to the upstream private repository and installs no model or application engine. The publisher validates app/help and copies it byte-for-byte into _site, adding only .nojekyll and a staging marker. It never publishes application data/, runtime/, weights, credentials, conversations or generated user outputs. Do not hand-edit _site or app/help; edit the sources in sources.json instead.

Automatic deployment#

.github/workflows/documentation.yml rebuilds on pushes to main and can also be started manually from Actions. Only _site is uploaded to the github-pages artifact and deployed by the official Pages action. Set repository Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source to GitHub Actions.

The root English README links to #/en/overview, and the French README to #/fr/overview; the reader's language selector remains available on both. Page and section links use hash routes so they work beneath a project Pages URL and from an offline file:// URL without server rewrites.

Embedded help#

The full app/help remains in the application distribution. F1 and Options keep opening its local file URL. Publishing introduces no network dependency into embedded help and does not replace it with a web link.

Public reader: Documentation.

pages.title: Local documentation (CyDoc)
pages.html:
Local documentation (CyDoc)#

The editable Markdown listed in sources.json remains the source of truth. build.py imports it into CyDoc with stable page IDs, local media, full operation schemas and a lexical index of the shipped app/tool.py. Original French guides are retained; absent translations are explicit and tracked. Do not hand-edit app/help.

From the application root (Node.js >=22 and npm are build requirements only):

sh
python app/documentation/build.py --installpython app/documentation/build.py --checkpython app/help_docs.py --page overview --locale en

--install installs the locked generator under runtime/documentation-build, outside the shipped application. Subsequent builds need no installation. An already built CyDoc checkout/package may be selected with --cydoc-root PATH.

The complete generated app/help/ is shipped with application/update archives. Open app/help/index.html through a file URL. F1 opens contextual help; Options provides manual and workspace buttons. No HTTP server, CDN, network request or Node.js is needed for reading. External reference links remain optional external navigation.

CyDoc is pinned in cydoc-source.json and distributed under MIT; its full notice is in this directory, app/help and root LICENCES. Preserve generated third-party notices. MeshStudio alone includes an original procedural GLB with the mesh module and Three.js. Other modules are selected from actual imported media. Unused module scripts are absent. No interactive graph, GIF decoder or video player is added merely because an application can produce that format.

Review app/help/migration-report.json for old/missing links and translation-report.json for missing/stale translations. SDK reference pages are labelled separately from actual application capabilities. Linux/macOS launchers remain unverified unless a validation report records an execution on those platforms.

Web documentation#

Documentation · Français. See Publishing the reader for the GitHub Actions workflow and local staging commands. Embedded help continues to work offline.

pages.title: CyDoc migration validation
pages.html:
CyDoc migration validation#

Scope#

Existing user/developer guides, local illustrations, shipped operation schemas and the public Python entry-point source were migrated. The original Markdown is retained as editable source and for GitHub links. App/help is generated and includes all reader resources. Node.js is required only for regeneration; the reader uses local classic scripts and file URLs.

Checks executed on Windows#

  • Pinned CyDoc 0.1.0 built from revision 774f2a7eabf7dd181a98ffc5add115b580b67f42.
  • App-local npm lockfile installation and full CyDoc build/check.
  • Python routing tests: English/French, legacy paths, Unicode, spaces/hash characters, media links, unknown page fallback, browser failure, active operation and common anchors.
  • Native ImGui test-engine clicks on both help buttons and F1, using the product interpreter. The browser call was intercepted to assert its file URL without launching tabs.
  • The full standalone Options window was opened and closed in an isolated application copy.
  • Generated reader tested in a DOM fixture with network calls forbidden: rendering, operation links/anchors, language switch and in-window image expansion/Escape when used.
  • The pinned CyDoc core, interactions and packed-asset suites passed (25 tests), including keyboard/pointer controls and reading-position restoration.
  • Distribution selections are checked for the entire help tree and notices.

Limits#

The automation browser blocks file URLs. A real browser visual check of file-origin storage, layout, codecs and WebGL remains necessary; DOM fixtures do not prove it. Linux and macOS were not executed. Touch-device behavior is covered by library interaction fixtures, not a physical touch-device run. Existing missing translations remain visible in translation-report.json. No model inference was needed or rerun for this migration. The migration report records old missing references; SDK reference documents may describe older SDK releases and are explicitly labelled separately from current operation contracts.

Regenerate and verify#

From the application root:

sh
python app/documentation/build.py --installpython app/documentation/build.py --checkpython app/tests/test_documentation.pypython app/help_docs.py --page overview --locale en --print-url

Existing release builders regenerate/validate the manual before packaging. When a builder uses git archive, commit the generated reader together with its source changes first. Keep the complete app/help directory and LICENCES/CyDoc-MIT.txt in the delivered product.

pages.title: CyTools_AudioLibrary — developer and integrator guide
pages.html:
CyTools_AudioLibrary — developer and integrator guide#

Documentation · Français

Standalone CyTool (cy.tool.audiolibrary, 0.1.3) built on CyToolsCore 0.10.1. Maintenance: Cyberalien. One runtime, one manifest (CyTool.json, generated by build_manifest.py), four façades: Dear ImGui, CLI, JSONL/HTTP, MCP. No dependency on CyToolsManager, on a GUI for the CLI/MCP paths, or on one AI client.

All commands below are run from the Tool root (the folder that holds CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe) in PowerShell. Every one of them was executed on the validation machine; results are in Docs/AudioLibrary-Validation.md.

Install#

The CyToolsCore SDK 0.10.1 (MIT) is installed by Install.ps1 from its public repository, at the exact commit pinned in app/requirements.txt, so git is needed from the first step. Moving to a newer SDK means changing that pin and running the tests again. Model weights are never part of the repository: they are downloaded from the Installation tab, or with install_model, into data\models\.

powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File app\Install.ps1            # base runtime: runtime\python.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\setup_backend.py            # AI engine: runtime\engines\torch + pinned sources.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\setup_backend.py --statuspowershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File app\build_launcher.ps1     # CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe (Visual C++ build tools)

The base runtime needs Python >= 3.11 on the machine (it creates the private environments at their final path). The engine is PyTorch 2.8.0 + cu126 (or --cpu-only), pinned in engine.json with a constraints file so that a dependency cannot replace the CUDA build. git is needed once for the engine sources.

Models#

powershell
.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke list_models.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke install_model --params '{\"modelKey\":\"laion-clap@htsat-unfused\"}' --timeout 7200

Models whose licence needs a personal acceptance (M2D-CLAP: NTT licence; Omni-Embed-Audio: Qwen Research backbone) fail with LicenseAcceptanceRequired until the user passes "acceptLicense": true — in the interface, by ticking the box themselves. An agent must ask the user; it must not set this flag on its own. A Hugging Face token (gated/private custom models only) is stored with .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\maintenance.py login (read from stdin, kept in the OS credential store, never in argv, jobs, settings or logs).

Model key Role Adapter State in this delivery
m2d-clap@2025 default audio/text embedding, zero-shot tags m2d_clap installed, validated
laion-clap@htsat-unfused legacy CLAP, second engine hf_clap installed, validated
omni-embed-audio@qwen3b-cl complex queries, negations omni_embed installed, validated (9.8 GiB VRAM peak)
qwen3-1.7b@2025-04 (default), qwen3-0.6b, qwen3-4b query understanding LLM, generic prompt hf_causal_lm 1.7B validated
cytools-search-assist@v1 (default), cymetasound-search-assist-0.5b@v1 query understanding, Qwen2.5 1.5B / 0.5B fine tuned on 4 753 messy queries, GGUF Q8_0 from Hugging Face, shared with CyMetaSound hf_causal_lm (ggufFile) installed from Hugging Face and validated, promptProfile: caption
m2d-clap@2024, omni-embed-audio@qwen3b-ac other versions of the same families same adapters not validated
audio-flamingo-3@hf deep captioning/reranking none declared extension point only

Custom model or new version: register_model (or Installation > Add a custom model). It is referenced in place; modelId@version + revision + weights hash + analysis settings form the analysis key, so each version keeps its own embeddings and index. A brand-new architecture needs one adapter file (adapters/base.py contract) referenced as file:<adapter.py>; nothing else in the Tool changes.

Recommended search setup (measured)#

Models for search VRAM Caption test, expected file first Query time (warm)
M2D-CLAP alone 0.75 GiB 3/5 (5/5 in the top 2) 0.02 s
M2D + LAION-CLAP (default for new Libraries) 1.4 GiB 4/5 0.03 s
+ Omni-Embed on GPU 10.3 GiB 4/5 0.1 s
+ Omni-Embed on CPU (its default device) 1.4 GiB, ~14 GB RAM 4/5 2-3 s (51 s first load)
Qwen3-1.7B assistant (Auto: long, non-English or negated requests only) +~3.5 GiB — +1.2 s
CySearchAssist 1.5B (GGUF Q8_0) +~3.4 GiB 92.0 % in the top 5 against 58.0 % raw, on 150 messy queries +3.4 s warm
CySearchAssist 0.5B (GGUF Q8_0) +~1.2 GiB 250/250 valid answers, weaker understanding of rare words +2.2 s warm

The default model for query understanding is the one named in the application settings (llmModel, Options or the LLM list of the search bar). It is the same default for the interface, the CLI and MCP: an assistant that calls search_sounds without naming a model gets the one you see on screen. The catalogue marks cytools-search-assist@v1 as the default assistant once it is installed (Installation tab).

The two CySearchAssist models are published as GGUF Q8_0 on Hugging Face (cyberalien/CySearchAssist-CLAP-1.5B and -0.5B) and read through transformers with the gguf package, so no second runtime is needed. Dequantising takes 35 to 45 s, so the first GPU load also writes the dequantised model to _dequantized/ next to the GGUF (2.9 GB and 0.9 GB); later loads read it in 1 to 2 s, and it is rebuilt if the GGUF changes. Quantisation costs a little: on the same 150 queries run on this machine, the 1.5B finds the right family in the top 5 for 94.0 % in float16 and 92.0 % in Q8_0.

The two prompt profiles#

A model declares, in its registry entry, which instruction it was trained for. generic is the built-in prompt with its few-shot examples, used by the Qwen3 entries. caption is the schema of the fine tune: one clean English caption, three variations, and suggested categories and tags. Giving a fine tune the generic prompt makes it answer worse, which is why the profile is declared rather than guessed, and why no code anywhere tests a model's name.

Suggested categories are hints, never a filter. Only the ones that exist in the Library's own taxonomy are used, as a re-ordering bonus on candidates the embeddings already found (hintBoost, 0.12 by default, 0 disables it). On 250 validation queries the bonus moved the expected family from 72.8 % to 87.2 % of first places. That number compares the model with the Library's automatic categories, so it measures agreement between two models rather than perceptual relevance.

Omni-Embed brought no measurable gain on this small test; keep it unticked for everyday searches and enable it for hard requests (negations, long descriptions). Installation > Device for this model sets a per-model device; indexing a Library with a model on CPU is much slower than on GPU, so index with GPU, then switch that model to CPU for searching. Models stay resident idleUnloadSeconds (default 300 s) after the last request, then all VRAM is released.

Use#

powershell
.\CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe                                            # interface.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py describe.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke create_library --params-file lib.json.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke scan_library --params '{\"libraryId\":\"<id>\"}' --timeout 36000.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke analyze_library --params '{\"libraryId\":\"<id>\"}' --timeout 360000.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke search_sounds --params-file search.json.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py --data-dir data\jobs-mcp mcp     # MCP stdio server

lib.json: {"name": "My SFX", "cacheLocation": "G:/CyToolsCache/AudioLibrary", "folders": ["D:/Audio/SFX", "E:/GameAudio"]}. One runtime per data directory: give the MCP server its own --data-dir (as above) when the interface is open. The Library database itself (SQLite WAL, in the cache) is shared safely between them. The one-shot CLI reloads models at each call; the interface and the MCP server keep them resident (idle unload after 300 s, idleUnloadSeconds in data/settings/audiolibrary.json).

MCP client entry (replace <tool> with the absolute path of the Tool root):

json
{"mcpServers": {"cytools-audiolibrary": {"command": "<tool>/runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe",  "args": ["<tool>/app/tool.py", "--data-dir", "<tool>/data/jobs-mcp", "mcp"]}}}

Using the Tool from an AI assistant (MCP)#

Typical split: the user builds and scans Libraries in the standalone; an assistant connected through MCP searches them and proposes sounds. The same Library files and caches are shared, so nothing has to be exported.

  • Find a sound: op_search_sounds with {"parameters": {"text": "heavy metal door slam, long reverb", "topK": 10}}. libraryId is optional: without it every Library is searched and each result carries libraryName, the absolute path of the original file, duration, tags, categories, a score per model and matchedSegment for long recordings. Poll cy_get_job until Completed, then read outputs.results. Any language works (llmAssist: auto).
  • More like this one: similarTo (+ libraryId). Narrow down with filters (duration, channels, type, category, tag...).
  • Manage on request: op_list_libraries, op_create_library, op_add_folder, op_check_library (read-only diff), op_scan_library, op_analyze_library, op_library_status, op_update_assets (user tags, categories, rating, favourite, description, notes).
  • Work folder by folder: op_list_folders returns the tree of a Library with recursive and direct file counts. A path from it becomes filters: {"rootIds": [rootId], "folderPrefix": "Impacts/Metal"} in op_browse_assets (the files) or op_update_assets (edit the whole folder in one call: addTags, removeTags, addCategories, removeCategories, appendNotes...). An empty filter is refused rather than read as "the whole Library".
  • Prepare files for another program: op_export_bundle copies audioIds, or everything filters match, into a destination folder (layout flat or folders, bundle.json listing source, AudioId, tags and categories). It only reads the originals, never overwrites, and refuses a destination inside a Library folder or a cache. In the interface, the same sounds can also be dragged out of the list (Windows, copy only) into Explorer or Unreal Engine.
  • op_install_model.acceptLicense, op_rename_files.confirm, op_undo_rename.confirm and op_write_metadata.confirm are the user's decisions: ask, show what will change, and only then pass true.

Background synchronisation (standalone)#

Each Library has autoSync = auto (default) | ask | off, autoSyncIntervalSeconds (300) and autoAnalyze (true), editable in the left panel (Automatic update) or with update_library. The window submits a read-only check_library job per Library at start-up and at each interval; when something changed, auto runs scan_library (then analyze_library for new/modified files when autoAnalyze), ask shows a banner with Update now / Ignore. Missing files are hidden, never purged; an unplugged drive is reported as unavailable. The MCP server has no timer: an assistant calls check_library itself.

File Tools (the only operations that change original files)#

suggest_names (read-only plan from category + tags for names like sound_01, ZOOM0012), rename_files (same folder, same extension, never overwrites, journalled), undo_rename, and write_metadata (ID3 for WAV/AIFF/MP3, Vorbis comments for FLAC/OGG/Opus, MP4 atoms for M4A; written into a copy, decoded audio verified identical, then swapped; backup in <cache>/Common/FileOperations/Backups; database identity refreshed so nothing is re-analysed). Audio files have no EXIF: these tag formats are the audio equivalent. BWF bext/iXML chunks (Soundminer-style) are not written in this version. mutagen (GPL-2.0-or-later) does the tagging; it is a dependency of the base runtime.

Test#

powershell
.\runtime\python\Scripts\cytools.exe validate app\CyTool.json.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s app\tests -v      # fixtures: no PyTorch, no weights.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\scripts\validate_real.py --models m2d-clap@2025 laion-clap@htsat-unfused --llm qwen3-1.7b@2025-04 --folders "C:/Windows/Media".\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\scripts\validate_mcp.py               # real MCP stdio client.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\scripts\scale_test.py --files 20000.\CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe --ui-test-library                                   # rendering proof in data\reports.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe runtime\bootstrap.py --ui-test-options --ui-test-language=fr

Release#

powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File app\build_launcher.ps1             # CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe, rebuilt from source.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\scripts\build_package.py            # every release asset, from the committed code

build_package.py writes runtime\build\release\<version>\: the user package (the committed files, LICENSE, LICENCES\ and the launcher), cytools-app.zip with its .sha256 (through build_release.py), and SHA256SUMS.txt. It refuses to run on uncommitted changes and stops if a licence file would be missing from the package.

The archive holds exactly the files the repository keeps under app/, plus LICENSE: the list comes from Git and .gitignore, so data, runtimes, model weights, the SDK wheel and local development files never enter it. It is checked with the application's own update code before the script reports success. Attach cytools-app.zip, cytools-app.zip.sha256 and the rebuilt launcher to the GitHub release; the Updates tab expects those names.

Architecture#

text
gui/ (ImGui)   tool.py (35 operations)   CLI / JSONL / HTTP / MCP        <- façades, same Runtime.submit        \____________ CyToolsCore Runtime: validation, jobs, sessions, scheduler, ledger ____________/audiolib/library    virtual Library = portable JSON; cache anywhere, movable, never beside the audioaudiolib/scanner    identity (size + fast hash, SHA-256 on demand): new/unchanged/modified/moved/missing/duplicateaudiolib/audiofile  libsndfile + PyAV decoding (no external ffmpeg), BS.1770 loudnessaudiolib/waveform   min/max peak pyramid, memory-mappedaudiolib/registry   model descriptors, capabilities, versions, receipts, analysis keysaudiolib/embeddings one store + one index provider per analysis key (flat exact cosine; pluggable)audiolib/search     per-model retrieval -> weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion; never mixes embeddingsaudiolib/llm        optional query understanding -> stable structured query; deterministic parser fallbackaudiolib/taxonomy   editable hierarchical taxonomy, zero-shot softmax labelling per modelaudiolib/modelhost  persistent engine worker (registered with Runtime.register_worker)audiolib/fileops    rename + write tags: the only code that changes original files (confirm, journal, verified copy, backup)worker.py + adapters/   the only code that imports PyTorch; runs in runtime/engines/torch

What the SDK lacked. CyToolsCore (0.9.0 when this was written, still so in 0.10.1) ships a one-shot ProcessWorker; a search cannot reload a model per query. audiolib/modelhost.py is a persistent JSONL worker with real cancellation (the process is killed and reaped before the job reports Cancelled) and idle unload. It uses the Core's own worker contract (register_worker, release, health), so it is not a second scheduler. A generic persistent worker with handshake/heartbeat would be a reasonable SDK extension; the adapters and the protocol verbs are Tool-specific.

Licences of every component: Options tab and licenses.json. Updates: Docs/UPDATES.md. Coverage of every requested capability: Docs/CapabilityCoverage.md. Evidence and limits: Docs/AudioLibrary-Validation.md.

CyTools_AudioLibrary is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public License, version 3 only (GPL-3.0-only), as published by the Free Software Foundation; the full text is in LICENSE at the root of the Tool. It is distributed WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY, without even the implied warranty of MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. The CyToolsCore SDK it is built on is under the MIT licence: its text and the sources of every component are in LICENCES/. The licence covers the application code: engines and model weights keep their own terms (licenses.json), and the non-commercial ones are downloaded by each user rather than distributed with the Tool.

Application icon#

The logo source is assets/branding/logo.png. build_icon.ps1 derives the 16-256 px Windows ICO and assets/app_settings/icon.png for Hello ImGui. build_launcher.ps1 embeds the ICO in the launcher. branding.py selects assets independently of the working directory and assigns this Tool its own Windows taskbar identity.

Modular CyUI#

The standalone interface uses the pinned, selected CyUI 1.2 modules. See the migration and validation notes for replacements, retained host adaptations, source hashes and reproducible refresh instructions.
pages.text: CyTools_AudioLibrary — developer and integrator guide # Documentation · Français Standalone CyTool ( cy.tool.audiolibrary , 0.1.3) built on CyToolsCore 0.10.1. Maintenance: Cyberalien. One runtime, one manifest ( CyTool.json , generated by build_manifest.py ), four façades: Dear ImGui, CLI, JSONL/HTTP, MCP. No dependency on CyToolsManager, on a GUI for the CLI/MCP paths, or on one AI client. All commands below are run from the Tool root (the folder that holds CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe ) in PowerShell. Every one of them was executed on the validation machine; results are in Docs/AudioLibrary-Validation.md . Install # The CyToolsCore SDK 0.10.1 (MIT) is installed by Install.ps1 from its public repository, at the exact commit pinned in app/requirements.txt , so git is needed from the first step. Moving to a newer SDK means changing that pin and running the tests again. Model weights are never part of the repository: they are downloaded from the Installation tab, or with install_model , into data\models\ . powershell Copy powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File app\Install.ps1 # base runtime: runtime\python .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\setup_backend.py # AI engine: runtime\engines\torch + pinned sources .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\setup_backend.py --status powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File app\build_launcher.ps1 # CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe (Visual C++ build tools) The base runtime needs Python >= 3.11 on the machine (it creates the private environments at their final path). The engine is PyTorch 2.8.0 + cu126 (or --cpu-only ), pinned in engine.json with a constraints file so that a dependency cannot replace the CUDA build. git is needed once for the engine sources. Models # powershell Copy .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke list_models .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke install_model --params '{\"modelKey\":\"laion-clap@htsat-unfused\"}' --timeout 7200 Models whose licence needs a personal acceptance (M2D-CLAP: NTT licence; Omni-Embed-Audio: Qwen Research backbone) fail with LicenseAcceptanceRequired until the user passes "acceptLicense": true — in the interface, by ticking the box themselves. An agent must ask the user; it must not set this flag on its own. A Hugging Face token (gated/private custom models only) is stored with .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\maintenance.py login (read from stdin, kept in the OS credential store, never in argv, jobs, settings or logs). Model key Role Adapter State in this delivery m2d-clap@2025 default audio/text embedding, zero-shot tags m2d_clap installed, validated laion-clap@htsat-unfused legacy CLAP, second engine hf_clap installed, validated omni-embed-audio@qwen3b-cl complex queries, negations omni_embed installed, validated (9.8 GiB VRAM peak) qwen3-1.7b@2025-04 (default), qwen3-0.6b , qwen3-4b query understanding LLM, generic prompt hf_causal_lm 1.7B validated cytools-search-assist@v1 (default), cymetasound-search-assist-0.5b@v1 query understanding, Qwen2.5 1.5B / 0.5B fine tuned on 4 753 messy queries, GGUF Q8_0 from Hugging Face, shared with CyMetaSound hf_causal_lm ( ggufFile ) installed from Hugging Face and validated, promptProfile: caption m2d-clap@2024 , omni-embed-audio@qwen3b-ac other versions of the same families same adapters not validated audio-flamingo-3@hf deep captioning/reranking none declared extension point only Custom model or new version: register_model (or Installation > Add a custom model ). It is referenced in place; modelId@version + revision + weights hash + analysis settings form the analysis key, so each version keeps its own embeddings and index. A brand-new architecture needs one adapter file ( adapters/base.py contract) referenced as file:<adapter.py> ; nothing else in the Tool changes. Recommended search setup (measured) # Models for search VRAM Caption test, expected file first Query time (warm) M2D-CLAP alone 0.75 GiB 3/5 (5/5 in the top 2) 0.02 s M2D + LAION-CLAP ( default for new Libraries ) 1.4 GiB 4/5 0.03 s + Omni-Embed on GPU 10.3 GiB 4/5 0.1 s + Omni-Embed on CPU ( its default device ) 1.4 GiB, ~14 GB RAM 4/5 2-3 s (51 s first load) Qwen3-1.7B assistant (Auto: long, non-English or negated requests only) +~3.5 GiB — +1.2 s CySearchAssist 1.5B (GGUF Q8_0) +~3.4 GiB 92.0 % in the top 5 against 58.0 % raw, on 150 messy queries +3.4 s warm CySearchAssist 0.5B (GGUF Q8_0) +~1.2 GiB 250/250 valid answers, weaker understanding of rare words +2.2 s warm The default model for query understanding is the one named in the application settings ( llmModel , Options or the LLM list of the search bar). It is the same default for the interface, the CLI and MCP: an assistant that calls search_sounds without naming a model gets the one you see on screen. The catalogue marks cytools-search-assist@v1 as the default assistant once it is installed (Installation tab). The two CySearchAssist models are published as GGUF Q8_0 on Hugging Face ( cyberalien/CySearchAssist-CLAP-1.5B and -0.5B ) and read through transformers with the gguf package, so no second runtime is needed. Dequantising takes 35 to 45 s, so the first GPU load also writes the dequantised model to _dequantized/ next to the GGUF (2.9 GB and 0.9 GB); later loads read it in 1 to 2 s, and it is rebuilt if the GGUF changes. Quantisation costs a little: on the same 150 queries run on this machine, the 1.5B finds the right family in the top 5 for 94.0 % in float16 and 92.0 % in Q8_0. The two prompt profiles # A model declares, in its registry entry, which instruction it was trained for. generic is the built-in prompt with its few-shot examples, used by the Qwen3 entries. caption is the schema of the fine tune: one clean English caption, three variations, and suggested categories and tags. Giving a fine tune the generic prompt makes it answer worse, which is why the profile is declared rather than guessed, and why no code anywhere tests a model's name. Suggested categories are hints, never a filter. Only the ones that exist in the Library's own taxonomy are used, as a re-ordering bonus on candidates the embeddings already found ( hintBoost , 0.12 by default, 0 disables it). On 250 validation queries the bonus moved the expected family from 72.8 % to 87.2 % of first places. That number compares the model with the Library's automatic categories, so it measures agreement between two models rather than perceptual relevance. Omni-Embed brought no measurable gain on this small test; keep it unticked for everyday searches and enable it for hard requests (negations, long descriptions). Installation > Device for this model sets a per-model device; indexing a Library with a model on CPU is much slower than on GPU, so index with GPU, then switch that model to CPU for searching. Models stay resident idleUnloadSeconds (default 300 s) after the last request, then all VRAM is released. Use # powershell Copy .\CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe # interface .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py describe .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke create_library --params-file lib.json .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke scan_library --params '{\"libraryId\":\"<id>\"}' --timeout 36000 .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke analyze_library --params '{\"libraryId\":\"<id>\"}' --timeout 360000 .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke search_sounds --params-file search.json .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py --data-dir data\jobs-mcp mcp # MCP stdio server lib.json : {"name": "My SFX", "cacheLocation": "G:/CyToolsCache/AudioLibrary", "folders": ["D:/Audio/SFX", "E:/GameAudio"]} . One runtime per data directory: give the MCP server its own --data-dir (as above) when the interface is open. The Library database itself (SQLite WAL, in the cache) is shared safely between them. The one-shot CLI reloads models at each call; the interface and the MCP server keep them resident (idle unload after 300 s, idleUnloadSeconds in data/settings/audiolibrary.json ). MCP client entry (replace <tool> with the absolute path of the Tool root): json Copy { "mcpServers" : { "cytools-audiolibrary" : { "command" : "<tool>/runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe" , "args" : [ "<tool>/app/tool.py" , "--data-dir" , "<tool>/data/jobs-mcp" , "mcp" ] } } } Using the Tool from an AI assistant (MCP) # Typical split: the user builds and scans Libraries in the standalone; an assistant connected through MCP searches them and proposes sounds. The same Library files and caches are shared, so nothing has to be exported. Find a sound: op_search_sounds with {"parameters": {"text": "heavy metal door slam, long reverb", "topK": 10}} . libraryId is optional: without it every Library is searched and each result carries libraryName , the absolute path of the original file, duration , tags, categories, a score per model and matchedSegment for long recordings. Poll cy_get_job until Completed , then read outputs.results . Any language works ( llmAssist: auto ). More like this one: similarTo (+ libraryId ). Narrow down with filters (duration, channels, type, category, tag...). Manage on request: op_list_libraries , op_create_library , op_add_folder , op_check_library (read-only diff), op_scan_library , op_analyze_library , op_library_status , op_update_assets (user tags, categories, rating, favourite, description, notes). Work folder by folder: op_list_folders returns the tree of a Library with recursive and direct file counts. A path from it becomes filters: {"rootIds": [rootId], "folderPrefix": "Impacts/Metal"} in op_browse_assets (the files) or op_update_assets (edit the whole folder in one call: addTags , removeTags , addCategories , removeCategories , appendNotes ...). An empty filter is refused rather than read as "the whole Library". Prepare files for another program: op_export_bundle copies audioIds , or everything filters match, into a destination folder ( layout flat or folders , bundle.json listing source, AudioId, tags and categories). It only reads the originals, never overwrites, and refuses a destination inside a Library folder or a cache. In the interface, the same sounds can also be dragged out of the list (Windows, copy only) into Explorer or Unreal Engine. op_install_model.acceptLicense , op_rename_files.confirm , op_undo_rename.confirm and op_write_metadata.confirm are the user's decisions: ask, show what will change, and only then pass true . Background synchronisation (standalone) # Each Library has autoSync = auto (default) | ask | off , autoSyncIntervalSeconds (300) and autoAnalyze (true), editable in the left panel ( Automatic update ) or with update_library . The window submits a read-only check_library job per Library at start-up and at each interval; when something changed, auto runs scan_library (then analyze_library for new/modified files when autoAnalyze ), ask shows a banner with Update now / Ignore . Missing files are hidden, never purged; an unplugged drive is reported as unavailable. The MCP server has no timer: an assistant calls check_library itself. File Tools (the only operations that change original files) # suggest_names (read-only plan from category + tags for names like sound_01 , ZOOM0012 ), rename_files (same folder, same extension, never overwrites, journalled), undo_rename , and write_metadata (ID3 for WAV/AIFF/MP3, Vorbis comments for FLAC/OGG/Opus, MP4 atoms for M4A; written into a copy, decoded audio verified identical, then swapped; backup in <cache>/Common/FileOperations/Backups ; database identity refreshed so nothing is re-analysed). Audio files have no EXIF: these tag formats are the audio equivalent. BWF bext /iXML chunks (Soundminer-style) are not written in this version. mutagen (GPL-2.0-or-later) does the tagging; it is a dependency of the base runtime. Test # powershell Copy .\runtime\python\Scripts\cytools.exe validate app\CyTool.json .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s app\tests -v # fixtures: no PyTorch, no weights .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\scripts\validate_real.py --models m2d-clap@2025 laion-clap@htsat-unfused --llm qwen3-1.7b@2025-04 --folders "C:/Windows/Media" .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\scripts\validate_mcp.py # real MCP stdio client .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\scripts\scale_test.py --files 20000 .\CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe --ui-test-library # rendering proof in data\reports .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe runtime\bootstrap.py --ui-test-options --ui-test-language=fr Release # powershell Copy powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File app\build_launcher.ps1 # CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe, rebuilt from source .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\scripts\build_package.py # every release asset, from the committed code build_package.py writes runtime\build\release\<version>\ : the user package (the committed files, LICENSE , LICENCES\ and the launcher), cytools-app.zip with its .sha256 (through build_release.py ), and SHA256SUMS.txt . It refuses to run on uncommitted changes and stops if a licence file would be missing from the package. The archive holds exactly the files the repository keeps under app/ , plus LICENSE : the list comes from Git and .gitignore , so data, runtimes, model weights, the SDK wheel and local development files never enter it. It is checked with the application's own update code before the script reports success. Attach cytools-app.zip , cytools-app.zip.sha256 and the rebuilt launcher to the GitHub release; the Updates tab expects those names. pages.title: CyTools_AudioLibrary
pages.html:
CyTools_AudioLibrary#

Documentation · Français

Maintenance: Cyberalien.

A desktop Tool to manage, analyse and search large local sound libraries. It references your folders without ever moving or copying the files, draws their waveforms, plays them, and lets you find a sound by describing it in any language: several audio embedding models (M2D-CLAP 2025, LAION-CLAP, Omni-Embed-Audio) search at once and their rankings are fused, and an optional small local LLM turns a messy request into clean captions first. Your own tags, categories, ratings and notes can be set on one sound, a selection or a whole folder. The same library can be searched by an AI assistant through MCP.

It runs as a Dear ImGui application, as a command line and as an MCP server, all on the same CyToolsCore runtime.

The user guide, in French, is LISEZ-MOI.md. The developer notes are in app/README.md, and what was measured, with its limits, in app/Docs/AudioLibrary-Validation.md.

Only Windows 10 with an NVIDIA card has been executed. The Linux launcher exists and has never been run.

Screenshots#

The library: folders, categories and quick filters on the left, the search bar and the sound list in the centre, then the player with its waveform and what each model found for the selected sound.

The analysis queue: progress of every stage and model, the analysis data kept per model version, and the editor of the categories and tag vocabulary.

What this repository contains, and what it does not#

The repository carries the application (app/), the user guide and the Linux launcher.

It does not carry:

  • model weights (data/models/, about 2 GB for the default search pair, about 26 GB with every catalogue model): installed from the Installation tab or with install_model, from the pinned catalogue in app/models/catalog.json. M2D-CLAP and the Omni-Embed-Audio backbone come under their own licences, the latter non-commercial, which each user accepts personally in that tab.
  • runtime/: the private Python of the application, the PyTorch engine, the pinned engine sources, staged updates and backups. It is rebuilt with the steps below.
  • your data (data/): libraries, caches, waveforms, embeddings, jobs, logs, settings and reports stay on your machine. Nothing is ever written next to your audio files, except by the two File Tools operations, which ask for confirmation.
  • the Windows launcher CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe: compiled from app/launcher.cpp.

From a release#

Download CyTools_AudioLibrary-<version>-windows-x64.zip from the releases, unzip it where the application should live (it creates its private environment in that folder), then run once, from that folder:

powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File app\Install.ps1.\CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe

Python 3.11 or newer and git are needed for that step; the launcher says so if it was skipped. cytools-app.zip and its .sha256, also attached to each release, are what the Updates tab of an installed copy downloads: they are not meant to be unzipped by hand.

From a clone#

Windows, PowerShell. Python 3.11 or newer and git must be on the PATH: the SDK is installed from its repository at the exact commit pinned in app/requirements.txt. These steps were executed on the development machine from a fresh clone, with Python 3.11: installation, the tests, and the interface started both through the launcher and through runtime\bootstrap.py. Building the launcher itself was not repeated there.

powershell
git clone https://github.com/MrMybal/CyTools_AudioLibrary.gitcd CyTools_AudioLibrarypowershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File app\Install.ps1           # private runtime in runtime\pythonpowershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File app\build_launcher.ps1    # CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe (Visual C++ build tools).\CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe

Without the Visual C++ build tools, start the same interface with .\runtime\python\Scripts\pythonw.exe runtime\bootstrap.py.

In the application, the Installation tab installs the AI engine (a private PyTorch environment, several GB) and the models, with their size, source and licence. Then create a Library, add your folders, scan, and search. app\Install.ps1 -Engine installs the engine from the command line instead.

From an AI assistant (MCP)#

json
{"mcpServers": {"cytools-audiolibrary": {"command": "<tool>/runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe",  "args": ["<tool>/app/tool.py", "--data-dir", "<tool>/data/jobs-mcp", "mcp"]}}}

Replace <tool> with the absolute path of the clone. The assistant can search every library, browse the folder tree, edit tags and notes, and scan or analyse on request. Installing a model under a personal licence, renaming files and writing tags into files always need your explicit yes: the operations refuse to run without it. Details in app/README.md.

Updates#

The Updates tab reads the releases of this repository. A release carries cytools-app.zip and cytools-app.zip.sha256, built by app\scripts\build_release.py. An update replaces app/ only, is verified before it is activated at the next start, keeps the previous version for a rollback, and never touches data/. Packages of the private Python environment, such as the CyToolsCore SDK, are not part of an application update: run app\Install.ps1 again to install the versions the new app/requirements.txt pins. The engine sources and the model weights are separate update streams.

Tests#

powershell
.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s app\tests -v   # no PyTorch, no weights.\runtime\python\Scripts\cytools.exe validate app\CyTool.json

The standalone interface uses the pinned, selected CyUI 1.2 modules. See the migration and validation notes for replacements, retained host adaptations, source hashes and reproducible refresh instructions.

pages.title: export_bundle
pages.html:
Copy a selection of sounds (audioIds) or every sound a filter matches into a folder the user chooses, for instance to prepare what a game engine or a DAW will import. The originals are only read. Nothing is ever overwritten: a file already present with the same content is left as it is, a different one with the same name gets a numbered name. A destination that would put copies inside a folder of any Library or inside a cache is refused. bundle.json lists every file with its source, AudioId, duration, tags and categories; exporting into the same folder again adds to it.

pages.title: search_sounds
pages.html:
Find sounds in the user's local audio Libraries from a free-text description in any language (or sounds similar to a known asset). Omit libraryId to search every Library at once. Each result gives the absolute path of the original file, duration, tags, categories, a 0-100 score per model and, for long recordings, the matching time segment: enough to propose sounds to the user. Each model retrieves from its own index; ranks are fused with weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion. The job is asynchronous: poll cy_get_job and read outputs.results when Completed.

Each result gives the absolute path of the original file, duration, tags, categories, a 0-100 score per model and, for long recordings, the matching time segment: enough to propose sounds to the user. Each model retrieves from its own index; ranks are fused with weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion. pages.title: write_metadata
pages.html:
CHANGES ORIGINAL FILES. Writes description, tags, categories, rating and AudioId into the files themselves (ID3 for WAV/AIFF/MP3, Vorbis comments for FLAC/OGG/Opus, MP4 atoms for M4A). Tags are written into a copy, the decoded audio is verified identical, then the copy replaces the original; a backup goes to the Library cache by default. Embeddings stay valid.

Contract#

json

Writes description, tags, categories, rating and AudioId into the files themselves (ID3 for WAV/AIFF/MP3, Vorbis comments for FLAC/OGG/Opus, MP4 atoms for M4A). Tags are written into a copy, the decoded audio is verified identical, then the copy replaces the original; a backup goes to the Library cache by default. Embeddings stay valid.",  "inputSchema": {    "type": "object",    "properties": {      "libraryId": {        "type": "string",        "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{8}$",        "description": "LibraryId returned by create_library or list_libraries"      },      "audioIds": {        "type": "array",        "items": {          "type": "string",          "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{32}$",          "description": "Stable AudioId of an asset (survives renames and moves)"        },        "minItems": 1,        "maxItems": 5000      },      "fields": {        "type": "array",        "uniqueItems": true,        "items": {          "type": "string",          "enum": [            "description",            "tags",            "categories",            "rating",            "audioId"          ]        },        "description": "Absent = all"      },      "includeAutoTags": {        "type": "boolean",        "default": true,        "description": "false = user tags only"      },      "backup": {        "type": "boolean",        "default": true,        "description": "Keep the untouched original in <cache>/Common/FileOperations/Backups"      },      "confirm": {        "type": "boolean",        "const": true,        "description": "Must be true. Source:   https://github.com/MrMybal/CyToolsCore
Revision: a8d200f2d0baaade1633e0683663b4506c595f74 (pinned in app/requirements.txt)

    app/tool.py
    app/ui_common.py
    app/generation_config.py

The application package contains no third-party code beyond the SDK files listed above.
The components below are downloaded on the user's machine, from their official sources,
when the user installs them. Each keeps its own licence; the Options tab of the
application and app/licenses.json list them, and the Installation tab shows the licence
of every model before it is installed.

pages.title: CyTools_AudioLibrary
pages.html:
CyTools_AudioLibrary#

Documentation · English

Bibliothèque audio locale intelligente : gestion, analyse, catégorisation et recherche en langage naturel dans de grandes collections de sons. Vos fichiers ne sont jamais déplacés, copiés ni modifiés (sauf si vous utilisez vous-même l'onglet Outils fichiers, voir plus bas) : une bibliothèque référence des dossiers, et tout ce que le Tool calcule (base, waveforms, embeddings, index) va dans un cache que vous placez où vous voulez.

Démarrer#

  1. Depuis une release GitHub : téléchargez CyTools_AudioLibrary-<version>-windows-x64.zip, décompressez-le là où l'application doit vivre (elle crée son environnement privé dans ce dossier), puis, une seule fois, ouvrez PowerShell dans le dossier décompressé et lancez : powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File app\Install.ps1 Il faut Python 3.11 ou plus récent et git. Les deux autres fichiers de la release (cytools-app.zip et son .sha256) servent à l'onglet Mises à jour : ne les décompressez pas à la main.
  2. Double-cliquez sur CyTools_AudioLibrary.exe (Linux : ./CyTools_AudioLibrary.sh, non testé). Si un message indique que le runtime privé est absent, c'est que l'étape 0 n'a pas été faite.
  3. Onglet Installation : installez le moteur IA (PyTorch privé, plusieurs Go), puis les modèles voulus. L'assistant de recherche CySearchAssist-CLAP-1.5B (1,6 Go, par défaut) ou sa version 0.5B (0,5 Go, plus légère) vient de Hugging Face, comme dans CyMetaSound. Pour un modèle dont la licence l'exige, lisez-la et cochez vous-même la case d'acceptation : le Tool ne l'accepte jamais à votre place.
  4. Onglet Bibliothèque : Nouvelle bibliothèque (nom + dossier du cache, par ex. G:\CyToolsCache\AudioLibrary), Ajouter un dossier autant de fois que nécessaire, Tout rescanner.
  5. Cochez les modèles à utiliser (panneau Modèles), puis Analyser la bibliothèque. L'onglet File d'analyse montre l'avancement et permet Pause / Reprendre / Annuler / Réessayer les échecs.
  6. Recherchez en langage naturel, dans n'importe quelle langue : « gros impact métallique très lourd avec une longue réverbération ». Cliquez un résultat : waveform, lecture immédiate, tête de lecture, informations, tags, catégories, score de chaque modèle et segment correspondant.

Vos tags, catégories et notes, sur un son, une sélection ou un dossier#

  • Un son : onglet Tags et catégories sous la waveform. Ajoutez ou retirez vos tags, choisissez une catégorie puis Ajouter la catégorie ou Retirer la catégorie, une note de 0 à 5, une description d'une ligne et des notes libres. Description et notes s'enregistrent seules, sans bouton.
  • Plusieurs sons : Ctrl+clic pour ajouter un son à la sélection, Maj+clic pour prendre toute une plage, Ctrl+A pour toute la liste, Échap pour vider. L'onglet devient Sélection (N) et chaque modification s'applique à tous : tags (chaque tag déjà présent affiche combien de sons le portent, et se retire de tous d'un clic), catégorie, note, favori, une ligne ajoutée aux notes de chacun sans effacer l'existant, et Analyser ces sons.
  • Un dossier : panneau gauche, la flèche d'un dossier ouvre ses sous-dossiers avec leur nombre de sons. Un clic affiche ce dossier et tout ce qu'il contient ; clic droit : Sélectionner tous les sons de ce dossier, Analyser ce dossier, Ouvrir le dossier. Sur un son de la liste, clic droit > Afficher seulement ce dossier.

Tout cela reste dans la base de la bibliothèque : vos fichiers audio ne sont pas modifiés. Pour renommer ou écrire les tags dans les fichiers eux-mêmes, onglet Outils fichiers, choix Les sons sélectionnés.

Sortir des sons de la bibliothèque : bundle et glisser-déposer#

  • Créer un bundle : onglet Sélection ou clic droit sur un son, Créer un bundle…, puis choisissez un dossier. Les sons y sont copiés, à plat ou en gardant leurs dossiers. Les originaux ne sont ni déplacés ni modifiés, et rien n'est écrasé : un fichier identique déjà présent est laissé tel quel, un fichier différent du même nom reçoit un nom numéroté. bundle.json liste chaque fichier avec sa source, ses tags et ses catégories ; refaire un bundle dans le même dossier le complète. Décochez bundle.json si vous importez ensuite tout le dossier dans un moteur de jeu. Un dossier situé dans une de vos bibliothèques ou dans un cache est refusé : les copies y seraient indexées.
  • Glisser-déposer : faites glisser un son, ou la sélection, hors de la fenêtre, vers l'Explorateur pour en faire des copies, ou vers le Content Browser d'Unreal Engine pour les importer dans le projet. Seule la copie est proposée : un glisser ne peut jamais déplacer ni effacer vos originaux.

Mise à jour automatique des bibliothèques#

Par défaut, l'application vérifie en arrière-plan (au démarrage puis toutes les 5 minutes) si des fichiers ont été ajoutés, modifiés ou retirés dans vos dossiers, et met la bibliothèque à jour toute seule, y compris l'analyse IA des nouveaux sons. Panneau gauche > Mise à jour automatique : Mettre à jour automatiquement, Me demander d'abord (un bandeau apparaît avec un bouton Mettre à jour maintenant) ou Désactivée. Les fichiers disparus sont masqués, jamais supprimés de la base : s'ils reviennent ou ont été déplacés, ils retrouvent leurs tags.

Utilisation par une IA (MCP)#

Une IA connectée au Tool peut chercher un son dans toutes vos bibliothèques (« trouve-moi une grosse porte métallique ») et vous proposer des fichiers avec leur chemin, et, si vous le lui demandez, créer une bibliothèque, ajouter un dossier, relancer un scan ou une analyse. Elle peut aussi parcourir l'arborescence de vos dossiers et traiter un dossier entier en une fois : ajouter des tags, une catégorie ou une ligne de notes à tous ses sons. Configuration : app/README.md.

Outils fichiers (modifient vos fichiers, uniquement à votre demande)#

  • Renommer les fichiers mal nommés (sound_01, ZOOM0012...) : le Tool propose un nom à partir de la catégorie et des tags ; vous cochez, corrigez si besoin, confirmez. Rien n'est écrasé, Annuler le dernier renommage existe, et les tags et analyses suivent le fichier.
  • Écrire les tags dans les fichiers (l'équivalent audio de l'EXIF : ID3, Vorbis, MP4) pour que d'autres logiciels les lisent. L'audio est vérifié identique avant de remplacer l'original, et une sauvegarde est gardée dans le cache.

Apparence#

Onglet Options : cinq thèmes (Gris moyen, par défaut, Gris clair, Nuit ambre, Violet, Bleu marine), densité Compacte ou Confortable et taille du texte. Le filtre actif, le dossier affiché et la sélection apparaissent en pastilles au-dessus de la liste : un clic sur la croix les retire. La barre du bas résume la bibliothèque et les tâches en cours.

Raccourcis#

Espace : lecture/pause · Haut/Bas : son précédent/suivant (Maj+Haut/Bas étend la sélection) · Ctrl+clic, Maj+clic, Ctrl+A : sélection multiple · Échap : vider la sélection · clic droit sur un son : Trouver des sons similaires · sur la waveform : molette = zoom, Maj+molette = défilement, clic = positionner, glisser = sélectionner (puis Boucler la sélection ou Trouver des sons similaires à la sélection).

Clic sur l'en-tête d'une colonne : trier la liste par nom, durée, type, catégorie, tags, dossier, état d'analyse et, dans les résultats d'une recherche, par score final ou par score d'un modèle ; un second clic inverse l'ordre. Dans les résultats, un troisième clic revient à l'ordre de pertinence de la recherche. Le son sélectionné reste sélectionné quand l'ordre change.

Où sont mes données ?#

Dossier Contenu
data/libraries définition portable de chaque bibliothèque (dossiers, cache, modèles, taxonomie)
cache choisi (défaut data/cache) base, waveforms, embeddings et index, par modèle et par version
data/models poids des modèles installés
data/logs, data/reports journaux et preuves de validation
app/ application (remplaçable par une mise à jour) · runtime/ : Python privé, moteur IA, mises à jour

Changer de modèle ou de version n'efface rien : les anciennes données restent jusqu'à ce que vous les supprimiez (onglet File d'analyse). Une réanalyse ne supprime jamais vos tags ni vos catégories.

Limites connues (version 0.1.3)#

Validé uniquement sur cette machine Windows 10 x64 + RTX 3090. Linux et macOS : jamais exécutés. L'installation utilise le Python du système pour créer les environnements privés : ce n'est pas un installeur autonome « sans Python ». Les mises à jour de l'application viennent du dépôt MrMybal/CyTools_AudioLibrary (onglet Mises à jour), mais aucune release n'y est encore publiée : le mécanisme n'a été testé qu'avec des archives de test. Audio Flamingo 3 est déclaré dans le registre mais n'a pas d'adaptateur. Détails, chiffres mesurés et preuves : app/Docs/AudioLibrary-Validation.md.

CLI, MCP et commandes développeur : app/README.md.

Maintenance : Cyberalien. Licence : GPL-3.0-only, texte complet dans LICENSE. Les moteurs et les poids des modèles gardent leurs propres licences, listées dans l'onglet Options.

Documentation locale#

Dans l’application, ouvrir Options → Ouvrir le manuel local (F1) ou appuyer sur F1. Le lecteur hors ligne complet est livré dans app/help/index.html. Régénérer le manuel.
